body:
Often times, I feel a bit lost while reading the documentation because
all the options' descriptions re collapsed, resulting in me considering
all the options with the same importance.

I feel like this is definitely something we want for templates &
cssClasses but some other options (even optional ones) are used a lot
and should be emphasized.

Before:

![screen shot 2016-11-23 at 10 16 45](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/29529/20556154/fa8d9416-b165-11e6-93d3-09a843778ae5.png)

After:

![screen shot 2016-11-23 at 10 17 07](https://cloud.githubusercontent.com/assets/29529/20556161/047ba74c-b166-11e6-8e25-42ae1ca657d1.png)

I'm still wondering if the `* Required` mention is required at the end; because I want some option to be "important" without putting them "required" (like `hitsPerPage` which has a default value of 20).

I therefore updated a few JSDocs snippets to remove the `[`...`]` optional notations.

Let me know what you guys think 👍

comments.body: By analyzing the blame information on this pull request, we identified @bobylito, @vvo and @PLNech to be potential reviewers
Some parameters from reading the jsDoc are now required (while they are not really required). Maybe we want to make them more visible without expressing they are required?

> Some parameters from reading the jsDoc are now required (while they are not really required).

Yes, that's what I was explaining. I want those ones to be emphasized and therefore removed the `[`...`]` JSdoc syntax to consider them "required" even if they have default values.
Arg, the parser has issues with default values of non-optional parameters; as soon as they're not integers. Will need to check how to improve that.

> Arg, the parser has issues with default values of non-optional parameters; as soon as they're not integers. Will need to check how to improve that.

I get this is maybe not even a bug, if the parameter is required there can't be a default value. It needs to be written as optionnal to be able to set a default value.

I've updated the parsing glitches @vvo.

> Maybe we want to make them more visible without expressing they are required?

Now yes, that's the main question. Do you have another idea to highlight important options with default values (that are theoretically optional)?

> Now yes, that's the main question. Do you have another idea to highlight important options with default values (that are theoretically optional)?

Maybe add a `*` at the end of the jsDoc parameter description then use this in the website generator to translate it to "important parameter"?

@vvo should be better now 👍
